messages:
maria: heads up — noticed a regression on long-context workloads when continuous-batching is enabled. memory climbs steadily and we see a stream of kvstore page faults and tiny evictions. occurs under batch-merge pressure (many small requests combined). cc @jonah @esther :thinking:

jonah: can you paste the pprof or flamegraph? also which model/seq len and batch settings?

maria: repro is with opt-2.7b, seq=16->2048 (simulated long context by chaining requests), continuous_batcher merge_threshold=8, max_batch=32. attaching short flame snippet:
```
(pprof) top 20
30.1%  runtime.kv_page_fault_handler
18.7%  runtime.kv_eviction_scan
12.4%  runtime.batch_coalesce
8.9%   runtime.kv_slot_reclaim
6.5%   runtime.attention_kernel_select
```
logs: (truncated)
[2026-03-10T14:02:10Z] batch-merge: id=0x7f4 merge_count=9, headwait=12ms
[2026-03-10T14:02:10Z] kv: page_fault shard=42 slot=891 evict=1
[2026-03-10T14:02:10Z] kv: reclaim slot=891 reused=false frag_left=128

maria: pattern looks like: when two batches with overlapping KV ranges merge, we end up tearing fragments and causing tiny evictions then re-alloc, which increases fragmentation and prevents reuse for later batches. tail latency also spikes (p95 -> p99 up ~40%).

esther: ugh. that matches the head-of-line blocking variant we saw earlier but not identical. did you see any "slot in use" asserts or version mismatches?

maria: no asserts, just reclaim/reuse=false in logs. I added KV_DEBUG=1 and got this sequence:
```
KV_DEBUG: alloc shard=42 slot=890 len=512 -> ok
KV_DEBUG: alloc shard=42 slot=891 len=64 -> ok
KV_DEBUG: merge batch: bA:{slots 880-900} + bB:{slots 890-910} -> performing split/handshake
KV_DEBUG: evict slot=891 (tiny) -> free -> alloc slot=891 len=4096 -> fragmentation++
```

jonah: so merge creates overlap and we do a split that forces tiny evict + immediate large alloc. that'll fragment. two immediate ideas: 1) avoid merging batches whose KV footprint overlaps beyond threshold; 2) change reclamation to prefer coalescing small adj fragments before reusing for large allocs.

esther: agree. also kernel selection interacts here: when we switch to the fused-attention kernel for long sequences we change memory access patterns which increases simultaneous live KV lanes => higher pressure. maybe the runtime should consider a merge-cost estimator that includes KV footprint delta.

maria: i measured metrics during the run: headlock_count jumped from ~120/min to ~380/min, kv_page_fault_rate x3, and memory RSS ~1.6x after steady state. attaching short CSV of metric deltas in case it's useful:
```
metric,baseline,regression
headlock_count,120,380
kv_page_fault_rate,0.6/s,1.9/s
p99_latency_ms,78,110
rss_mb,3200,5120
```

jonah: nice. does disabling continuous batching (or setting merge_threshold=999) remove the regression?

maria: yes, disabling merges removes the thrash but latency per-token increases (no batching). so we need a middle ground.

esther: i can run a microbench with deterministic sequences and an instrumented allocator. propose a quick experiment matrix: merge_threshold={4,8,16}, overlap_limit_slots={0.1,0.25,0.5} (fraction of combined footprint). we'll measure page_faults, frag_ratio, and tail latency.

jonah: also consider a cheap fast-path for small merges: if combined alloc needed > max_free_chunk then skip merge or reorder batches to avoid head-of-line. could be a heuristic: if overlap_fraction > X OR expected_alloc_growth > Y then don't merge.

maria: good heuristic. temp fix: i've pushed a canary that gates merges with overlap_limit_slots=0.25 for canary hosts in us-west. observing metrics now. deploy-bot: can you paste the canary id?

deploy-bot: Canary 2026-03-10-usw-merge-gate deployed at 2026-03-10T15:10:02Z to 5 nodes.

maria: early numbers after 30m: headlock_count down ~45%, page_faults down ~50%, p99 back within ~10% of baseline. but we still see some fragmentation growth over hours.

jonah: that's promising. long-term we should fix allocator/coalescer to avoid tiny evict+large alloc churn. i'll open an RFC issue with proposed allocator changes and a test harness for microbench. esther — can you run the experiment and attach the results?

esther: on it. running now with a 6h run for each cell, uploading results to /internals/perf/kv-merge-experiments/2002468100. attaching run command for reproducibility:
```bash
# deterministic client (seq lengths file) + instrumented runtime
./bench_client --model opt-2.7b --seq-file seqs/long_chains.txt --concurrency 8 --continuous-batcher --merge-threshold=8 --overlap-limit=0.25
./run_runtime --kv-debug --allocator=instrumented
```

maria: thanks. i created a bug: https://issues.redwood.ai/INF-7212 and assigned to @jonah. tagging for prioritization: perf/priority-high :fire: :100:

ci-bot: CI note — the canary config change touched the batching config; integration tests passed: 482/483 (one flaky).

maria: summary + action items: 1) esther runs experiment and uploads CSVs (in progress). 2) jonah to draft allocator RFC + test harness. 3) maria to monitor canary for 24h and roll if stable. 4) temporary merge gating config rolled to canary. will follow up with perf graphs tomorrow.

jonah: ok. if esther's tests confirm, i'll add a unit test that simulates overlapping KV footprints and asserts no fragmentation regression.

esther: ETA ~8h for first set of results.

maria: thanks everyone. filing a short postmortem entry if we need it after full run.

deploy-bot: Canary 2026-03-10-usw-merge-gate completed step: monitoring (30m) — all nodes healthy.
